idea.description: SASRec predicts the next interaction using causal self-attention over a user's item history. Item and position embeddings pass through attention and feed-forward blocks; the resulting features score candidate items through shared item embeddings. Training uses positive next items and sampled negatives. Source: [Self-Attentive Sequential Recommendation](https://arxiv.org/html/1808.09781v1).
idea.motivation: Attention can emphasize recent interactions in sparse histories while retaining access to older relevant actions. The supplied task establishes SASRec as the starting baseline; it does not specify a new cold-start mechanism. ID-based SASRec alone cannot learn useful representations for items absent from training.
idea.implementation_notes: Retain RecHarness sasrec_perdataset and routing for all four categories. Use preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], and the environment's SASREC_EPOCHS default of 200. Keep splits and host evaluation unchanged; select using macro validation HR@10. Store artifacts beneath the trial directory and keep predictor generation consistent with trained checkpoints. Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and the supplied compatibility contract. Any proposed content extension must use only permitted public metadata and requires validation; no benchmark improvement is established here.
idea.pseudocode:
For each category:
  Load unchanged RecHarness splits and item mapping.
  Initialize SASRec with seed 42.
  For each training batch:
    Embed padded item sequences and positions.
    Apply causal attention and feed-forward blocks.
    Score positive next items and sampled negatives.
    Minimize binary cross-entropy over valid positions.
  Save checkpoints and architecture configuration beneath the trial directory.
Generate working/predict.py with matching architecture and category routing.
Use the pinned host validation protocol to compare trials by macro HR@10.

originality.positive: The original paper introduced an influential attention-based approach to sequential recommendation.
originality.negative: Relative to the required RecHarness baseline, the supplied idea adds no concrete architectural or training innovation. Scores use a 1–10 scale.

future_potential.positive: Permitted titles and descriptions could support a separately validated extension for sparse item histories.
future_potential.negative: Such an extension is unspecified, and its benefit under the fixed evaluation and search budget is unknown.

code_difficulty.positive: Starting from the existing SASRec implementation makes baseline integration relatively straightforward; higher scores indicate greater difficulty.
code_difficulty.negative: Architecture changes require synchronized checkpoint loading, predictor generation, dataset routing, and diagnostic adapters.

report:
Matched RecHarness Amazon task: four datasets Movies_and_TV,
Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics, CDs_and_Vinyl, macro-average validation
HR@10. Start from RecHarness sasrec_perdataset. Preprocessing seed=0 and training
seed=42, exactly as run2.sh. The host executes your train.py and then independently
evaluates working/predict.py using the pinned RecHarness benchmark (200 validation
users/category, 99 unique negative candidates, evaluation seed=42). Test labels and
test metrics are unavailable during search. Retain all four categories and dataset
routing. DATA_DIR must remain os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; write artifacts beneath
your trial directory, as the baseline does. Training may change model architecture,
loss, optimizer, sampling and hyperparameters, as in RecHarness. Do not alter input
splits, invent metrics, read hidden test files, fetch extra datasets/pretrained weights,
or change the host evaluator. Changes to inference must also update the predictor
writer so working/predict.py loads the trained architecture. Keep execution single-GPU;
the host provides four concurrent trial slots and 64 CPU cores. No shell actions,
filesystem inspection, or training tools are needed in the LLM call: return code.
All training, diagnostics, debugging and failed trials consume the method's shared
43,200 GPU-second search budget. LLM time and final held-out inference are recorded
separately, matching run2.sh's separate final-evaluation step.
The original RecHarness tools layer sets SASREC_EPOCHS=200 (overriding the template's
standalone default of 300); this same environment default applies here.
